summary: Lincoln County, OR tower: 100-foot tower erected 1941 or 1942 (sources differ), a 34-foot tower in 1965, abandoned 1968, high winds in 1971; FFLA lists it as gone.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists the tower as gone; a 1971 newspaper item says high winds were apparently too much for it, without describing the damage
facts.agency: Lincoln County Fire Patrol Association (firelookout.com lists the Oregon Dept. of Forestry)

events.note: Rex's page lists a 100' tower with 7x7' cab in 1941
Association annual report labeled 1942 says the 100-foot tower was erected that year
Manned from April 11 for emergency fire detection; a permanent lookout from April 25 until September 29
Association report: a lookout tower constructed at a cost of $1067.58. Rex's page: a 34-foot live-in tower built from the bottom half of the Norton Hill lookout
The lookout made three first discoveries that season
Lincoln County Leader item (January 28, 1971): recent high winds apparently were too much for the lookout tower; damage not described

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rex's page dates the 100-foot tower to 1941; the association annual report labeled 1942 says it was erected that year. The story gives both dates.
Rex's page lists the Oregon Dept. of Forestry; the Forest Lookouts page and the association reports name the Lincoln County Fire Patrol Association. Both are given.

notes_for_editor: Most detail comes from association annual reports and newspapers as transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page; the originals were not checked. The 1965 tower is called a 34-foot live-in tower built from the bottom half of the Norton Hill lookout by Rex's page. The Norton Hill record says its tower moved to Euchre in 1965 according to one source and was dismantled and salvaged in 1967 according to another, so the two stories should be read together. The 1938 association entry (steel ladder, 6 x 6 cage, '100 foot tree lookout') is unclear about what it describes and is not used. The 30.5 m height matches the 100-foot tower. No current condition, access, visit or rental information found; the story says so. Only one WebSearch run was used for this tower; an orww.org PDF copy of the same article appeared in search results but was not read.
